title: Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia: Long or short accountability?
summary:
Market Hang tackles the top stories of the day. Including Nvidia's board unanimously reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO and what the White House's involvement says about accountability in corporate America, whether the government has effectively put a floor under the AI trade, and Anthropic falling as options on the stock begin trading for the first time.

The panel, with Yahoo Finance's Julie Hyman, debates where everyone sits on a one-to-five bullishness scale, whether this is a stock picker's market or a CapEx bubble that precedes a secular bear, the risk of a politically driven slowdown in data center construction, and OpenAI's chief scientist calling for a speed limit on AI development, including whether an FDA-style regulator is the right model for AI.

title: Jensen Huang back at Nvidia, stock soars; Anthropic slides
summary: The 8:30 team is joined by Roundhill Investments Chief Investment Strategist Drew Pettit to discuss why washed-out sentiment doesn't mean a fundamental bottom, his $50-to-$250 bull-bear range on Anthropic, and how to handicap the "Jensen premium" coming back into Nvidia. Deirdre Bosa Live host Deirdre Bosa also joins to break down Silicon Valley's reaction to Huang's return and what it means for the AI trade.

title: Mark Zuckerberg Has Collected Nearly $2 Billion in Dividends From the Stock He Started in a Dorm Room. It Now Pays Him About $2 Million a Day
summary: Mark Zuckerberg's latest Form 4 shows 341,117,213 Meta shares that earn the company's $2.10-a-share dividend: $716 million a year, about $2 million a day, from a payment Meta did not make until March 2024. He has collected $1.95 billion of it so far, before tax, while his salary stays at $1 and the stock sits 23% below its September high.
